proven_source_facts: Each Runtime constructs its own ReusableMemoryPool and borrows its execution stream. allocateMemory delegates to that pool, then creates a shared Memory owner wrapper.

Memory deleter captures shared Runtime. Memory destruction returns the block to that Runtime. Same-owner release returns to the pool without a stream drain; foreign-owner release first drains the Runtime stream.

Original HC Work allocates Tensor objects and holds all allocations in a vector; its destructor syncs before vector destruction. The existing explicit pre return drain is retained. Returned collapsed/post/comb Tensor handles independently share their own Memory and survive Work destruction.
The SDK pool header explicitly documents cached-block reuse/capture-cache-miss behavior. A warm HC Tensor::empty call cannot be equated to an unconditional fresh device malloc/free.

Current Runtime public API has no generic owner-scoped scratch slot or execution-resource retirement callback. Graph allocation leases serve graph lifetime; they do not provide an eager HC scratch retirement hook.

one_TU_design_boundary.safe_outputs: collapsed/post/comb remain independently allocated, never scratch-backed; retaining outputs across alternating inputs must not alias a later call.
one_TU_design_boundary.strong_TLS_or_global_cache: Cached Tensor -> shared Memory -> deleter shared Runtime. Keeping Tensor wrappers across calls keeps the Runtime alive past engine cleanup. A weak Runtime key does not fix the strong value chain. This conflicts with existing collection-before-destroy checks.
one_TU_design_boundary.weak_only_cache: Weak Tensor/Memory entries do not retain scratch after Work destruction, so they do not remove the next wrapper allocation.
one_TU_design_boundary.raw_blob_or_to_blob_bypass: Would require external memory/owner lifecycle and explicit cleanup integration; cannot safely infer retirement from raw Runtime pointer or reuse after address recycling. Not introduced.
one_TU_design_boundary.Runtime_attached_strong_Tensors: Would introduce a Runtime -> Tensor -> Memory -> Runtime ownership cycle unless a separate explicit cleanup/retirement mechanism is implemented. Existing API provides no such cheap eager hook.
